expectation: Membrane ring on activated or tissue-resident T cells, some NK and B cells. In gut mucosa it should be common: scattered single cells in the lamina propria and intraepithelial lymphocytes, plus denser groups in lymphoid aggregates. Unstained epithelium and stroma in between.
observed: A: villous gut mucosa outlined in yellow, with background glow. B, C: distinct ringed single cells in the lamina propria and between epithelial cells, epithelium dark. D: membrane rings around nuclei. E1: many ringed cells. E2: CD19 shows no cells.
why: Clear membrane rings on a distinct subset of scattered lymphocytes in the lamina propria and epithelium, as expected for tissue-resident cells; the background glow is separate from the cells.
notes: CD69 marks ringed lymphocytes scattered through the lamina propria and between epithelial cells, with the epithelium itself dark. Row E tells us nothing because CD19 shows no cellular structure. The glow in the whole-tissue view is an artefact and does not change the verdict.
